drivingQuestion: Why did the Sages forbid insulating food in non-heat-adding material after dark and in heat-adding material even by day?
outcomeNote: Rava answers each of Abaye's challenges

segments.he: [אָמַר] רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אֵין טוֹמְנִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוֹסִיף הֶבֶל מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁכָה? — גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יַרְתִּיחַ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת נָמֵי נִיגְזַר?! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סְתָם קְדֵירוֹת רוֹתְחוֹת הֵן.
segments.en: «And Rava said: Why did they say» that «one may not insulate» hot water even «in something that does not add heat», but only retains the pre-existing heat, «from nightfall» on Friday? It is «a decree lest one» come to «boil» the pot on Shabbat. «Abaye said to him: If so», if it is due to concern that one may boil it, then «during twilight we should also issue a decree» and prohibit insulating in something that does not add heat. Rava «said to him:» During twilight, there is no reason to be concerned because at that time «most pots are boiling,» as they have just been taken off of the fire. Later at night the pots cool down and it is conceivable that one may come to boil them in order to restore the heat.

segments.he: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אֵין טוֹמְנִין בְּדָבָר הַמּוֹסִיף הֶבֶל וַאֲפִילּוּ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם? — גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יַטְמִין בְּרֶמֶץ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ גַּחֶלֶת. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְיַטְמִין? גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יְחַתֶּה בַּגֶּחָלִים.
segments.en: «Why did» the Sages «say» that «one may not insulate» hot water for Shabbat «in something that adds heat, even while it is still day?» It is «a decree lest one come to cover it in hot ashes that contain» a glowing «ember.» People may not differentiate between addition of heat by means of hot ashes and other additions of heat. «Abaye said to him: Let him insulate» it with hot ashes, what is the problem? Rava answered him: It is «a decree lest one come to stoke the coals» in order to make them burn on Shabbat and thereby violate a Torah prohibition.
